features.cap: White, smooth to silky, 3–10 cm
features.underside: Free gills, pink when young, turning chocolate brown
features.stipe: Short and white, thin ring that often falls away, no volva
features.habitat: Grass, lawns and pastures, summer to fall

lookalikes.tell: The Destroying Angel has white gills, a white spore print and a sac-like volva at the base. Always dig up the whole base.
The Yellow-staining Mushroom turns bright chrome-yellow when you cut the stem base and smells of ink or phenol. The Meadow Mushroom smells pleasant and doesn't stain yellow.

features.cap: Pure white, smooth, 3–10 cm
features.underside: White, free, crowded gills that stay white
features.stipe: White, skirt-like ring, base sits in a sac-like volva that is often buried
features.habitat: Woods with oak, birch or pine, eastern North America, summer to fall

lookalikes.tell: The Meadow Mushroom has pink to brown gills, no volva, and grows in open grass.
Young Amanitas start as a white egg. Slice it top to bottom: any outline of a cap and gills inside means Amanita, not puffball.

features.cap: Egg-yolk to orange-yellow, wavy edge, becomes funnel-shaped
features.underside: Blunt, forked false gills (ridges) running down the stem
features.stipe: Solid, same colour as cap; flesh pulls apart like string cheese
features.habitat: On soil near hardwoods or conifers, singly or scattered, summer to fall

lookalikes.tell: The Jack-o'-Lantern has sharp true gills, grows in dense clusters on wood or buried roots, and is orange all the way through.
The Lobster Mushroom is red-orange, hard and heavy, with a pimply crust, bumpy ridges instead of forked ones, and white flesh inside.

features.cap: Bright orange, convex then funnel-shaped
features.underside: Sharp, crowded true gills running down the stem; can glow faintly in the dark
features.stipe: Orange, tapering, bases fused together in clusters
features.habitat: Dense clusters on hardwood stumps or buried roots, often oak, eastern North America

lookalikes.tell: Chanterelles have blunt forked ridges instead of sharp gills, grow singly from soil, and have white flesh inside.

features.cap: Honeycomb of pits and ridges, yellowish to tan, joined to the stem at its bottom edge
features.underside: No gills or pores; the pitted cap carries the spores
features.stipe: White; cut lengthwise, cap and stem form one continuous hollow chamber
features.habitat: Spring, near dying elm, ash, old apple orchards and tulip poplar
features.other: Must be cooked; raw morels make people ill

lookalikes.tell: The False Morel has brain-like lobes instead of pits, and is stuffed with cottony fibres when cut, not hollow.

features.cap: Brain-like wrinkled lobes, reddish-brown, no true pits; hangs loose like a skirt
features.underside: No gills or pores
features.stipe: Cut lengthwise it is chambered or stuffed with cottony fibres
features.habitat: Spring, conifer forests and sandy soil

lookalikes.tell: True morels have honeycomb pits and are completely hollow from cap tip to stem base.

features.cap: 7–20 cm, brown centre breaking into shaggy scales over white
features.underside: White, free gills that stay white
features.stipe: Smooth, double-edged movable ring, bulb at base; flesh bruises orange-red when cut
features.habitat: Compost, gardens, wood chips and conifer litter
features.other: Upsets some people's stomachs. North American finds are often the close relatives C. brunneum or C. olivieri.

lookalikes.tell: The Green-spored Parasol's gills turn greyish-green with age and it drops a green spore print. Always take a print.

features.cap: Large, white with brownish scales
features.underside: Gills white at first, turning greyish-green when mature
features.stipe: White with a movable ring
features.sporePrint: Green to greyish-green: the key feature
features.habitat: Lawns and grassy areas, often in fairy rings, commoner in warm regions
features.other: The most common cause of mushroom poisoning in North America

lookalikes.tell: The Shaggy Parasol drops a white spore print and its gills stay white.

features.cap: Honey-yellow to brown, fine dark hairs or scales near the centre
features.underside: Whitish to pinkish gills, attached or running slightly down the stem
features.stipe: Cottony ring, bases fused together in clusters
features.sporePrint: White; caps below often dusted white
features.habitat: Clusters on wood and roots of hardwoods, fall; a tree parasite
features.other: Must be well cooked; some people react

lookalikes.tell: The Deadly Galerina is smaller and drops a rusty-brown spore print instead of white.

features.cap: Small, 1–4 cm, sticky, tan to brown, fades paler as it dries
features.underside: Brownish attached gills
features.stipe: Thin and brownish, fragile ring zone stained rusty by spores
features.habitat: Decaying wood, often conifer, spring and fall
features.other: Contains the same amatoxins as the Death Cap

lookalikes.tell: Honey Mushrooms are bigger, have hairy caps, and drop a white spore print.

features.cap: Brown, bun-shaped, smooth and slightly greasy
features.underside: Pores, white then yellow to olive, not bruising blue
features.stipe: Thick and club-shaped, fine white net pattern on the upper part
features.habitat: With conifers and birch, summer to fall

lookalikes.tell: The Bitter Bolete has pinkish pores and a coarse dark-brown net on the stem.

features.cap: Tan to brown, smooth
features.underside: Pores white at first, becoming pinkish
features.stipe: Coarse dark-brown net pattern
features.habitat: Hemlock and hardwoods, often near rotting stumps
features.other: Intensely bitter; one mushroom ruins a whole dish

lookalikes.tell: The King Bolete has white to olive pores and a fine pale net on the stem.

features.cap: Red to yellow-orange with white or yellowish warts (volva remnants)
features.underside: White, free gills
features.stipe: White with a ring; bulb at base ringed with concentric bands of volva tissue
features.habitat: With conifers and birch, summer to fall
features.other: Eastern populations are often yellow-orange (var. guessowii)

lookalikes.tell: The Death Cap has a smooth olive-green cap, usually without warts, and a large sac-like volva.

features.cap: Olive-green to yellowish bronze, smooth, sometimes one white patch
features.underside: White, free gills
features.stipe: White, skirt-like ring, large sac-like cup (volva) at base
features.habitat: Introduced; under oak and pine, especially on the West Coast

lookalikes.tell: The Fly Agaric has a red or yellow-orange cap covered in warts and ringed bands at the base rather than a sac.
Young Amanitas start as a white egg. Slice it top to bottom: any outline of a cap and gills inside means Amanita, not puffball.

features.cap: Overlapping shelves, bright orange on top with yellow edges
features.underside: Sulphur-yellow tiny pores
features.stipe: None; attached directly to the wood
features.habitat: Oak and other hardwoods, summer to fall
features.other: Eat only young and cooked; some people react

lookalikes.tell: Hen of the Woods is a grey-brown rosette of small spoon-shaped caps with white pores.

features.cap: Rosette of many grey-brown spoon-shaped caps
features.underside: White pores
features.stipe: Branched white base joining all caps
features.habitat: Base of oaks, fall, eastern North America

lookalikes.tell: Chicken of the Woods has bright orange shelves with yellow pores.

features.cap: Large white ball, 10–50 cm, smooth leathery skin
features.underside: None; no gills, pores or stem
features.stipe: None; attached by a cord
features.sporePrint: Olive-brown; inside turns yellow then powdery with age
features.habitat: Meadows, lawns and woodland edges, late summer to fall
features.other: Only edible when solid pure white inside, like marshmallow

lookalikes.tell: A young Amanita 'egg' shows the outline of a cap and gills when sliced top to bottom. A puffball is uniform white inside.

features.cap: Shell or fan-shaped, white to grey-brown, in overlapping clusters
features.underside: White gills running down to the base
features.stipe: Short and off-centre, or absent
features.habitat: Dead hardwood, cool seasons from fall to spring

lookalikes.tell: Lion's Mane has hanging icicle-like spines instead of gills, and no cap.
Angel Wings are thinner, smaller and pure white, and grow on rotting conifer wood rather than hardwood.

features.cap: No cap; a white mass of hanging spines
features.underside: Icicle-like spines 1–5 cm long
features.stipe: None; attached to wood
features.habitat: Wounds on living hardwoods, especially oak and beech, fall

lookalikes.tell: Oyster Mushrooms have fan-shaped caps with gills underneath.

features.cap: Pure white, thin, fan or ear-shaped, 2–10 cm, in overlapping groups
features.underside: Narrow, crowded white gills
features.stipe: None, or a tiny stub
features.habitat: Rotting conifer wood, especially hemlock, late summer to fall
features.other: Linked to deaths in Japan in 2004, mainly in people with kidney disease

lookalikes.tell: Oyster Mushrooms are thicker and fleshier, often grey to brown, and usually grow on hardwood.

features.cap: Bright orange-red crust over a twisted, funnel-shaped mushroom
features.underside: No real gills, only blunt bumpy ridges where the gills used to be
features.stipe: Thick, same colour as the cap; flesh white and firm
features.habitat: On soil in mixed woods, summer to fall
features.other: A mould that covers a Russula or Lactarius host. Pimply surface. Skip any that are soft, mouldy or smell off.

lookalikes.tell: Chanterelles are yellow-orange with forked ridges, a fruity smell and stringy flesh, and have no pimply crust.

features.cap: White and smooth, can turn greyish and squarish with age, 5–15 cm
features.underside: Free gills, pale pink then chocolate brown
features.stipe: White with a thick ring; base turns bright chrome-yellow when cut
features.habitat: Lawns, parks, gardens and wood edges, often in groups; introduced, most common in the West
features.other: Unpleasant ink or phenol smell, strongest in the cut stem base

lookalikes.tell: The Meadow Mushroom is smaller, smells pleasant and doesn't stain yellow at the base.
The Horse Mushroom smells of anise or almond and only yellows slowly on the cap, not bright yellow in the stem base.

features.cap: Large, white to cream, smooth, slowly bruises yellowish, 8–20 cm
features.underside: Free gills, greyish pink then dark brown; young veil has a cogwheel pattern
features.stipe: White, large two-layered ring, no volva
features.habitat: Pastures and grassy places, often in rings, summer to fall

lookalikes.tell: The Yellow-staining Mushroom smells of ink or phenol and turns bright chrome-yellow in the cut stem base.
The Destroying Angel keeps white gills, has a white spore print and a sac-like volva at the base.

features.cap: Golden-brown to brown fibrous scales on a pale background, 10–25 cm
features.underside: Free gills, whitish then pinkish then dark brown
features.stipe: Tall, shaggy below a large ring, bruises yellow
features.habitat: Disturbed ground, roadsides and conifer woods, mainly in the West, summer to fall

lookalikes.tell: The Yellow-staining Mushroom has a smooth white cap without brown scales and smells of ink or phenol.
